transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (AE), Diego Ramos (SE), Zara Patel (Enablement), Sofia Martinez (Brightline Head of AI), Ethan Wu (Platform), Maya Singh (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Practice lab focused on demo flow, competitive rebuttals and security threads. Did three mock vignettes, called out failure modes, and codified fallback lines.

Topics planted in deck: demo hook, latency vs cost narrative, dedicated vs hosted decision tree, security quick answers. Links shared: Deck: /drive/enablement/se-storyline-2025.pdf, Sec FAQ: /drive/security/redwood-sec-faq-2025.pdf

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00:05] Avery: All right let's get started, thanks everyone for joining. Quick note: this is a practice with Brightline messaging in mind, so think of the customer persona as a regulated healthtech company with latency SLAs.
[00:00:22] Diego: Hey, I've got the demo vm up, we'll run the three vignettes—search assistant, triage summarizer, then a live prompt with a long context. We'll do a cold start and a warm cache run.
[00:00:36] Zara: Two housekeeping things, one record's on, and two the goal is to lock a 6-minute pitch + a 3-minute demo vignette for customer-facing reps.
[00:00:48] Speaker 2: Cool.
[00:01:10] Avery: Opening hook practice—option A is product-first: "Redwood gives you predictable per-token economics for production inference so you can ship features without surprise bills." Option B is pain-first: "If your models slow during peak triage windows, we fall back to compatible variants automatically and keep latency SLOs." Thoughts?
[00:01:35] Sofia: Pain-first resonates more with ops folks but for execs start with economics. Maybe a two-liner: cost + reliability.
[00:01:52] Diego: Agree. We should mention Dedicated briefly: "reserved capacity" vs "burst to hosted" as a quick line.
[00:02:06] Avery: Good — we'll refine. Ok vignette one: triage summarizer. Diego, take it away.
[00:02:20] Diego: (demo noise) All right feed in a 2,000 word clinical note and ask for a bulleted triage summary. Output's returned in 1.2s on warm cache, 3.8s on cold start for this model and config.
[00:02:46] Ethan: Wait those numbers—what instance and model are you using?
[00:02:52] Diego: Using rdx-7B-quantized variant on a single T4-ish node for demo; these are lab numbers, not SLA.
[00:03:05] Maya: When they ask about data residency—do we say hosted is okay or push private?
[00:03:12] Avery: Quick answer: hosted for non-PHI is fastest; for PHI or regulated data, recommend Private (VPC/on-prem) and cite KMS/HSM + audit logs. We should have a short script: "We support Private deployments with customer-managed KMS and full audit logs; we also offer dedicated clusters for predictable throughput."
[00:03:36] Diego: Note: some transcripts swap acronyms so be careful—say 'customer-managed KMS' rather than 'cust KMS'
[00:03:49] Speaker 1: ha yep
[00:04:20] Avery: Let's role-play competitor pushback: customer asks "Why not Anthropic or OpenAI?" Diego, you play prospect.
[00:04:29] Diego: Okay. "Why Redwood when Anthropic has Claude and a big safety story?"
[00:04:35] Avery: Short rebuttal: "Anthropic and OpenAI focus on model innovation; Redwood's differentiation is serving — we give you predictability and control for production inference (latency, cost, private deployments, and rollout controls) so your product doesn't get blocked by operational surprises."
[00:04:55] Sofia: Can you give a concrete example—like a rollback story?
[00:05:02] Diego: Sure. We demoed a canary where a version drifted; Redwood's automatic fallback to a verified variant kept pages under SLA while the team rolled back.
[00:05:15] Avery: Callout—rebuttal should include metrics: percent uptime improvement and token-cost delta if we have it. If not, say 'measurable reduction in per-token cost via batching and KV cache'.
[00:05:32] Zara: For sales decks, avoid sounding like "we're cheaper" — instead "cost controls and predictable economics."
[00:05:44] Ethan: On quantization — customers worry about accuracy regressions. What's the script?
[00:05:51] Diego: Script: "We validate quantized variants on your evals and provide quality monitoring. If the quantized model degrades on your critical prompts, we won't force the switch — we recommend the variant meeting your accuracy threshold."
[00:06:10] Maya: Good. Include 'eval hooks' in the pitch.
[00:06:22] Avery: Next vignette: a live long-context prompt—simulate a 25k token patient record. We'll show prefix caching and streaming.
[00:06:38] Diego: Streaming demo: when streaming is enabled, first token latency is X, throughput looks Y; the UI shows tokens gradually. (demo) Warm cache yields 0.9s first token, cold 2.7s.
[00:06:55] Sofia: Those numbers are great but we need to tie to user impact—"time to triage" or "time to insight" messaging.
[00:07:05] Avery: Exactly. Messaging: "Redwood reduces time-to-insight by mitigating cold starts and caching common prefixes."
[00:07:18] Speaker 3: Noted
[00:07:50] Diego: Quick friction: when customers press on private vs dedicated we often ramble. Let's script a crisp decision tree: 1) Need PHI/data residency => Private. 2) Need predictable throughput + cost => Dedicated. 3) Low security needs + cost flexibility => Hosted.
[00:08:12] Maya: Can we add 'timeline to deploy' numbers? Customers ask that first.
[00:08:17] Avery: Yes — Hosted: minutes to hours; Dedicated: weeks for capacity and SLA provisioning; Private (VPC or on-prem): weeks to months depending on entitlements. We'll add ranges.
[00:08:29] Diego: Also mention integrations: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS.
[00:08:38] Avery: Okay vignette three — live Q&A flow where model hallucination is surfaced and we do a graceful degradation.
[00:08:55] Diego: (demo) We purposefully prompt with ambiguous instruction; model hallucinates a citation. Then we show Redwood's rerank + fallback policy: switch to a higher-precision variant or synchronous retrieval. That keeps output within guardrails.
[00:09:20] Ethan: Customers always ask for evidence—do we show logs?
[00:09:24] Avery: Yes show trace: per-token latency, route selected, model variant, and audit entry—show a sample log line. Link to example log in the Sec FAQ.
[00:09:36] Zara: Quick note on phrasing—avoid "hallucination" with some execs; prefer "unsupported assertion" or "confidence mismatch."
[00:09:48] Sofia: That's helpful, we prefer 'unsupported assertion' in clinical reviews.
[00:10:05] Diego: Role-play: buyer says "Your cost sounds lower but what about vendor lock-in?"
[00:10:12] Avery: Reply: "We avoid lock-in via open model compatibility and exportable KV caches; customers can snapshot model states and migrate to another runtime if needed. Our SDKs are standard and your prompts/labels remain portable."
[00:10:32] Ethan: Pushback: "But if you optimize kernels and compilers, isn't that lock-in?"
[00:10:38] Diego: Acknowledge: "We do runtime optimizations but keep model artifacts and prompts portable; migration requires some ops work but we provide migration guides and tooling."
[00:10:50] Avery: Let's test a rapid-fire objection set. Diego toss objections, Avery answer in 20 seconds.
[00:11:05] Diego: "What about model freshness?"
[00:11:09] Avery: "We support pinned versions and rolling update policies to minimize drift, and can run shadow traffic for validation before switching."
[00:11:20] Diego: "Is there SLA for latency?"
[00:11:24] Avery: "Dedicated customers can get latency SLAs; hosted has SLOs but not SLA for free-tier accounts."
[00:11:34] Diego: "How do you handle PII/PHI in logs?"
[00:11:38] Avery: "We offer redaction hooks, ensure audit logs don't include raw prompt text by default for regulated deployments, and provide optional encrypted audit trails for SOC2 customers."
[00:11:55] Zara: That last line should reference a doc: /drive/security/audit-redaction-guidance.pdf
[00:12:10] Speaker 4: (mumble)
[00:12:42] Avery: Trainer note — we practiced the flow but stumbled on the migration/lock-in story. Diego, you mentioned offering migration guides—can you draft a 1-page migration summary?
[00:12:56] Diego: Yep I'll draft it, include steps for KV export, model artifact export, and prompt inventory extraction.
[00:13:10] Avery: Audience handling, quick tips: 1) Mirror the customer's top KPI in the first 30s. 2) Use a two-line tech + business pitch. 3) Have an explicit fallback demo in case the live model trips.
[00:13:30] Sofia: For healthtech, mention regulatory posture first — that gets the room's attention.
[00:13:37] Avery: Good.
[00:14:05] Diego: Now let's do a cold-start failure rehearsal. I'll simulate a network spike and force the fallback.
[00:14:12] (sound of keyboard, demo)
[00:14:38] Diego: Cold start induced—response time spikes and then we auto-route to smaller variant with a brief note: "Switched to verified small-variant to keep latency within SLOs."
[00:14:58] Maya: Customers will ask if that affects accuracy—have a line: "We identify critical prompts and pin them to variants that meet accuracy bar; non-critical prompts can be auto-routed for cost savings."
[00:15:18] Avery: Great — that line is now in script.
[00:15:45] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[00:16:10] Diego: Quick training micro-tip: avoid heavy kernel talk with product managers; focus on outcome (latency/cost/uptime). Use 'kernel optimizations' only with infra owners.
[00:16:28] Avery: Let's switch to competitive narrative against Cohere—Cohere often markets large models and embeddings. Our angle: unified inference controls + quantization profiles for production.
[00:16:50] Diego: Also mention Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching / quantization suggestions tailored to their workloads.
[00:17:05] Sofia: Can you give a soundbite for execs: 15 seconds?
[00:17:09] Avery: "Redwood is the inference control plane that helps teams keep APIs fast, costs predictable, and compliance intact—so product teams ship with confidence."
[00:17:25] Maya: Nice.
[00:17:55] Diego: A few dev-level FAQs pulled up: how to configure autoscale policies, how batching impacts p99, and how to surface regressions.
[00:18:10] Avery: Walkthrough on the console already prepared—trace view, token breakdown, and per-route latency.
[00:18:28] Diego: Instruction: show a token-level cost breakdown live; customers like seeing per-token numbers tied to a sample request.
[00:18:41] Zara: Also add a small slide that explains 'what we mean by predictable economics' with a before/after example.
[00:18:58] Avery: Closing role-play: run the 6-minute demo end-to-end. Diego you'll narrate tech, I'll handle business tie-ins, Zara will note chops.
[00:19:12] (demo run noise)
[00:25:30] Diego: End of run — timing 6:05 including Q&A. Missed the migration line once.
[00:25:42] Avery: Good, notes: shorten the warm-up hook by 10s, add migration CTA mid-demo. We'll capture exact script changes.
[00:25:55] Maya: Two wrap asks from Brightline POV: 1) show SOC2 + audit log sample, 2) trial plan for dedicated capacity.
[00:26:10] Avery: We'll provide both links and a trial outline.
[00:26:30] Zara: Next steps recap — see action items.
[00:26:45] Avery: Any final quick objections we didn't cover?
[00:26:50] Sofia: Nothing from me. This was helpful.
[00:27:02] Diego: One last practice tip: always confirm the customer's definition of "latency SLO" early in the call.
[00:27:15] Avery: Great. Thanks all — we'll circulate updated script and security bundle. End recording.
